meta.title: How a Cache Works
meta.outro: Ask the copy first, the source only on a miss.

scenes.narration: A cache keeps a copy of slow answers close by. The first request pays, every request after it is fast.
scenes.title: How a Cache Works
scenes.lede: Keep a copy of slow answers close, so the next request is fast.
tldr: **Hit:** the answer comes from the copy
**Miss:** read the source once, then keep a copy

scenes.heading: One request, three steps
scenes.narration: The app asks the cache first. If the cache does not have it, it reads the database. Then it keeps a copy, so the next ask is a hit.
badges: On a miss, read the database
Keep a copy for next time

scenes.heading: Hit or miss
scenes.narration: A hit is fast. A miss costs one database read. A stale copy is the risk, so every entry gets an expiry time.

cells: Read the database, then store a copy
Copy is older than the source

scenes.heading: Where the time goes
scenes.narration: Across a thousand requests, the misses cost more than all the hits together. Illustrative numbers.

scenes.heading: What to do
scenes.narration: Cache reads that repeat. Give every entry an expiry. Watch the hit rate.

points.title: Give every entry an expiry
points.body: A TTL bounds how stale a copy can be.

points.title: Watch the hit rate
points.body: Below about 80 percent, the cache is not paying for itself.
